verdict: both defensible (curator: per-experiment curve; agent: paper's combined envelope); GT additionally carries a 0.27 dex unit defect
my_readings: Supp. Fig. 3 CASPEr-ZULF-Comagnetometer region boundary: log10 g_aNN[GeV^-1] ~ -2.5 at m=1e-22 eV, -2.9 at 1e-21, -3.2 (flat) over 1e-20..1e-17 eV -> canonical g_an = 2 m_n g_aNN ~ 1.2e-3 flat. nEDM region below it at log g_aNN ~ -4.6 over 3e-20..1e-17 eV (g_an ~ 4.7e-5). Main-text Fig. 3 green line = lower envelope of all corrected regions.
evidence: Agent points: 1.75e-3 @1e-22, 1.0e-4 @1e-20, 4.0e-5 @1e-18 (= nEDM floor), i.e. the combined 'Stochastic' envelope of main Fig. 3. GT: 1.2e-3 @1.2e-22, 6.0e-4 flat @1e-20..1e-17 = the CASPEr-comag curve alone, but stored as the raw repo file in GeV^-1 (PlotFuncs multiplies CASPEr_Comagnetometer.txt by 2*m_n at plot time; GT header absent, benchmark labels it 'g_an (dimensionless)'), so GT is 0.27 dex below canonical. Residual 1.39 dex is dominated by the nEDM-vs-CASPEr curve choice (~1.1-1.4 dex over 1e-19..1e-17).
policy_question: For a re-analysis paper that corrects several experiments and plots a combined envelope, does the compilation want the per-experiment corrected curve (curator) or the paper's headline combined envelope (agent)?
notes: Agent read the supplement and knew the envelope merged nEDM+CASPEr+sidebands; it did not consider emitting the per-experiment curve. Secondary REF: GT units (GeV^-1 vs dimensionless, x2m_n).

verdict: agent right (matches the paper's Fig. 5); curator file does not match this paper's figure
my_readings: Fig. 5 solid black MICROSCOPE line: |d_e| flat at ~2.2e-4 from 1e-24 eV up to ~1e-13 eV, then rises, reaching d_e~1e-2 near 8e-12 eV and d_e~1 near 2e-11 eV. Text: D_e = 0.00027 d_e^2 from the D_mtilde=0 subspace.
evidence: Agent: 2.34e-4 flat, rise to 1.3e-2 @8.3e-12, 0.86 @2.2e-11 (faithful). GT (ScalarPhoton/MICROSCOPE.txt, repo cites 1712.00483): 1.08e-4 flat, rise starting ~3e-14 eV, 0.11 @2.6e-12, 1.6 @4e-12 -> 0.33 dex lower plateau and rise ~0.5 dex earlier in mass; p90 2.2 dex. The GT shape/normalisation resembles a re-derivation (e.g. Hees et al. 2018 style, d_e~1e-4) rather than Berge et al.'s own Fig. 5.
notes: Median 0.32 just over threshold; tail from the rise position. Agent considered and rejected the Yukawa alpha(lambda) and dilaton (D_mtilde,D_e) planes, correctly.

verdict: both defensible: multi-coupling paper; agent emitted the SN1987A dark-photon bound (faithful to Fig. 3), benchmark GT holds only the red-giant scalar bounds (ScalarElectron/ScalarNucleon)
my_readings: Fig. 3 (SN1987A dark photon, eps vs m/MeV): floor of the black region ~5e-8 @0.1 MeV, ~5e-9 @1 MeV, ~4e-10 @10 MeV, resonant dip to ~1e-10 at 10-20 MeV, ~2e-10 @100 MeV, closing at ~400 MeV near 1e-8; ceiling ~1e-4..1e-7.
evidence: Agent: 5e-8 @1.05e5 eV, 4.4e-9 @1.02e6, 1.1e-10 @1.02e7, 6.8e-11 @2.0e7, 2.3e-10 @1.03e8, 5.6e-9 @3.98e8 (matches my reading within ~0.1 dex). GT files exist only for ScalarElectron/RedGiants.txt (flat 4.7e6) and ScalarNucleon/RedGiant.txt; no DarkPhoton or VectorBL file, so no comparison was possible.
policy_question: Which of the paper's several new bounds (RG/HB/solar scalar-electron and scalar-nucleon, solar B-L, SN dark photon) is 'the' limit; the compilation kept the stellar scalar bounds and credits the SN dark-photon curve elsewhere.

verdict: both defensible but not comparable: agent emitted the paper's headline QCD-sector combination Q_N.d (Fig. 3) under ScalarNucleon; benchmark GT holds the paper's alpha and m_e couplings (Fig. 4), which are canonical planes
my_readings: Fig. 3 caption: exclusion on Q_N.d = 0.999 d_gs + 0.092 d_mhat + ... (nucleon-mass modulation, values ~1e5..1e11, M_Pl = 2.4e18 GeV reduced); Fig. 4: exclusion of the coupling to (a) alpha and (b) m_e; abstract headlines the quark/gluon couplings.
evidence: Agent: 89 pts 3.2e5 @4.4e-14 .. 2.5e11 @4.2e-7 eV in Q_N.d, declared 'coupling (dimensionless)'. GT: ScalarPhoton/I2.txt (1.8e4 @1.3e-13 .. 5.5e8 @1.3e-7) and ScalarElectron/I2.txt (2.4e5 @1.3e-13 .. 9.8e8 @1.2e-7). policy_question: Whether the compilation records the paper's headline (QCD-sector) coupling, which has no canonical plane in the task card, or the alpha/m_e couplings it also reports and which the compilation stores.
notes: Transcript shows no consideration of emitting Fig. 4's d_e/d_me instead; the task card's 'pick the main result' rule points to Fig. 3, the compilation to Fig. 4.

verdict: agent right (Exp. B is the paper's exclusion); curator digitised Exp. A, which the paper says is not a valid exclusion
my_readings: Fig. 2(a) bottom panel (g_gamma [eV^-1] vs m): Exp. B (red) ~5e-23 at 1e-9 eV, ~2e-22 at 1e-8 eV, ~1e-20 at 4e-7 eV; Exp. A (purple) lies 0.5-0.8 dex below Exp. B over the whole range. Text p.3: Apparatus A has thousands of unexcluded spurious peaks, 'we cannot establish a good UDM candidate exclusion at these points'; A limits 'represent the ultimate apparatus sensitivity'.
evidence: Agent (d_e = g_gamma/kappa, kappa=2.906e-28 eV^-1): 1.8e5 @8e-10, 1.25e6 @1.5e-8, 3.7e7 @4e-7 -> Exp. B. GT (CsCav.txt): 2.2e4 @1.3e-10, 1.8e5 @1e-8, 3.6e7 @2.2e-7: uniformly ~0.7 dex below agent = Exp. A curve. Signed residual med +0.71 (agent above GT) with p90 1.05.
notes: Conversion d_e = g_gamma * M_Pl/sqrt(4pi) checked: 3.44e27 eV, consistent. Agent explicitly considered and rejected Exp. A.

verdict: both defensible: agent emitted the paper's own new dark-photon dispersion bound (Fig. 6 dashed green, Eq. 35); curator stored the B-L DM-stability region (cyan, Gamma > H0) from Fig. 5, which is a side constraint
my_readings: Fig. 6 dashed green delta m_e^earth line: eps ~1e-11 at 1e-20 eV rising with slope 1 (Eq. 35: g_e < 3.3e-12 (m/1e-20 eV) -> eps = g_e/e = 1.1e-11 (m/1e-20 eV)); black dashed Z line slope 2. Fig. 5 (B-L): cyan region 'DM stability (Gamma_gamma' > H0)' at g_B-L ~1e-16 for m ~ 2-4 eV, plus the same dashed dispersion lines.

Different coupling type and different physics; no comparison possible.

notes: Agent notes mention the Z-line alternative; they do not mention the B-L stability region.

verdict: agent right (reproduces Fig. 5 blue region to <0.1 dex); curator file is a uniform factor ~3.2 (0.51 dex) below the paper's Fig. 5
my_readings: Independent vector extraction of Fig. 5 blue fill (figure_5.pdf, identical in v1 and v2): lower boundary g_B-L = 1.1e-25 @4.2e-19, 3.6e-26 @1.6e-18, 6.2e-27 @3.2e-18, minimum ~8.9e-28 @~5e-18, 1.2e-26 @1.24e-17, 3.7e-24 @5.9e-17, 8.6e-23 @4.6e-16, 6.0e-23 @4.1e-15 eV.

verdict: both defensible: agent took the 0.1 B low-energy-SN contour (tightest), curator the 1 B normal-CCSN contour
my_readings: Fig. 3 two 'Energy deposition' contours. 1 B (thick): floor ~1e-8 @1 MeV, ~1.5e-9 @10 MeV, ~5e-10 @100 MeV, tip at ~465 MeV; ceiling ~3e-5 @10 MeV, ~2e-6 @100 MeV. 0.1 B (thin): floor ~5e-9 @1 MeV, ~3e-10 @100 MeV, tip at ~560 MeV; ceiling above 1e-4 up to ~150 MeV.

policy_question: Which of the two SN energy-deposition scenarios (normal CCSN E_dep<1 B vs low-energy SN E_dep<0.1 B) is the compilation's curve; the abstract advertises both ('even tighter bounds obtained from low-energy SNe').
notes: Agent explicitly noted the 1 B alternative in its notes.

verdict: both defensible; agent traced the smooth lower envelope (Fig. 1 'schematic'), curator stores the actual spiky per-bin limit (Fig. 2 data); agent did not consider Fig. 2
my_readings: Fig. 2 spiky limits (G395 blue 0.47-0.78 eV, G235 orange 0.78-1.4 eV, G140 green 1.4-2.55 eV) have lower envelope ~1.1-2e-11 GeV^-1 with spikes up to ~5e-11; Fig. 1 (captioned 'Schematic of our combined limits') is that lower envelope: ~2.2e-11 @0.6 eV, ~1.2e-11 @1 eV, ~1.1e-11 @1.5 eV, ~8e-12 @2.3 eV.
evidence: Agent: 2.2e-11 @0.59, 1.23e-11 @1.04, 1.15e-11 @1.41, 7.7e-12 @2.31 (= Fig. 1 envelope). GT (224k points): typical values 2.4e-11..5.4e-11 (spiky); comparing a lower envelope with a spiky reference at every reference mass gives a systematic +0.35 dex (median 0.36, p90 0.62). Transcript shows no inspection of Fig. 2 / G395 data.
policy_question: Whether the compilation curve is the paper's smoothed 'schematic' lower envelope or the raw spiky line-by-line limit (which the curator stores).
notes: An envelope is optimistic at almost every mass; a careful physicist would likely emit the spiky curve or its running median, so this could also be argued as P (traced a schematic instead of the result figure).

verdict: agent right on mass placement (h*f of the frequency axis matches the abstract's 4796.7-4799.5 MHz); curator followed the figure's internally inconsistent top mass axis

verdict: both defensible: agent reports the geometric centre of the thick BBN band, curator sits at/above its upper edge (consistent with the text formula f_a m_a > 1.3e-9 GeV^2)
my_readings: Fig. 1 left, BBN band edges by vector extraction (axes calibrated on tick labels): at m=1.07e-16 eV upper edge g_d=3.3e-19, lower 1.4e-19 GeV^-2; at 1 eV upper ~2e-3, lower 1.2e-3. Text bound f_a m_a > 1.3e-9 GeV^2 with g_d ~ 3.7e-3 GeV^-1/f_a gives 2.8e-19 @1e-16 eV and 2.8e-3 @1 eV.

policy_question: Which edge/centre of a deliberately thick (factor ~2.3, 40% g_d uncertainty) exclusion band the compilation records.
notes: Agent documented the band width and its centre choice.

verdict: both defensible: paper reports three channels (solar CBRD, solar 57Fe, galactic ALP DM); agent chose galactic ALP DM (Fig. 4), benchmark GT is the solar envelope (Fig. 3) after the #598 repointing
my_readings: Fig. 3: solid red CBRD limit flat at ~4e-12 for m<1 keV (figure; text says 4e-13 but LUX line drawn at ~3e-12 and 'similar to LUX' -> text is a typo), 57Fe dotted min ~6e-14 @10 keV. Fig. 4 galactic ALP red curve: ~1.2e-13 @1 keV, ~1.4e-13 @3 keV, ~2.5e-13 @4-5 keV (127Xe bump), ~2e-13 @10 keV, ~4e-13 @25 keV.

verdict: both defensible: Eq. 3.3 bounds a g_an/g_ap combination; agent projected onto g_ap (KSVZ discussion), curator onto g_an; numbers agree with the equation on both sides
my_readings: Eq. (3.3): g_an^2 + 0.61 g_ap^2 + 0.53 g_an g_ap <= 8.26e-19 -> g_an <= 9.09e-10 (g_ap = 0) or g_ap <= 1.16e-9 (g_an = 0); text quotes g_ap <~ 1.2e-9 for KSVZ. Bound is mass independent in the free-streaming regime.
evidence: Agent: AxionProton flat 1.164e-9 over 1e-12..1 eV. GT (AxionNeutron/SN1987A.txt): 9.0885e-10 flat (plus trapping ceiling 5.2e-7) over 1e-23..1 eV = sqrt(8.26e-19). The repo's AxionProton/SN1987A.txt cites 2306.01048, so the benchmark has no AxionProton GT for this paper.
policy_question: Which single canonical coupling a combined g_an/g_ap bound is projected onto when the compilation keeps only one of them for this paper.
notes: Task card allows either projection ('report the bound on the single canonical coupling with the other set to zero'); the choice is not fixed by the paper.

verdict: agent right; agent and curator sample the same noisy limit band, the residual is reference-sampling noise
my_readings: Fig. 3: five 300-kHz datasets, limit is a dense noisy band 1e-8..5e-8 GeV^-1 with spikes to 1.5e-7, typical ~1.5-2e-8 (caption: average sensitivity 1.9e-8). Mass 40.9-43.3, 49.3-50.6, 54.4-56.7 neV.

Comparing a smoothed median with individual noisy vertices yields median 0.30 dex (threshold), signed median -0.16, p90 0.56. No systematic offset.
notes: Borderline miss (0.304 dex). Any smoothing of a noisy per-bin limit is penalised by a scorer that interpolates at every noisy reference vertex.

verdict: both defensible: agent took the standard-cosmology curve (blue dashed), curator the most conservative variant (blue solid, extra Delta N_eff and xi_nu_e)

verdict: both defensible: agent emitted the union boundary of all cosmological regions in Fig. 1, curator stores each region (x_ion, EBL, XRAY, ...) as a separate file

verdict: curator's choice (photon-only coupling panel) fits the g_agamma plane better; agent chose the hypercharge-coupling panel and rescaled by cos^2(theta_W); both curves are in the paper

verdict: agent right (traced the observed spiky curve of the Fig. 9 inset); curator stores a flat headline value 4e-13 and the scorer compared at the single surviving reference mass at the window edge

verdict: both defensible: agent emitted the NFW-conservative bound quoted in the abstract, curator stored the generalized-Hernquist optimistic (max-D-factor) column of the ancillary file

verdict: both defensible; agent traced the paper's main-result Fig. 4 (R_em = 4 R_s, gamma_sp = 2.3), curator's file matches the conservative Fig. 5(a) (R_em = 1e4 R_s) to ~0.3 dex; agent did not consider Fig. 5

policy_question: Which DM-spike emission-region assumption (R_em = 4 R_s main result vs the conservative R_em = 1e4 R_s check) the compilation adopts.
notes: If the curator's intent was Fig. 4, this would instead be a 2-dex REF defect; the closeness to Fig. 5(a) makes POL more likely.

verdict: both defensible: the paper (title: 'Axion and dark photon limits from Crab Nebula') reports both; agent chose the ALP-photon exclusion, compilation stored only the dark-photon one (Crab_2.txt)
my_readings: Fig. 3 (ALP): 95% C.L. exclusion contour with floor ~1.6-1.8e-10 GeV^-1 over 2e-7..6e-7 eV (text: g < 1.8e-10 for m = 2e-7..6e-7 eV), rising to ~1e-9 at 6e-8 and 1.4e-6 eV. Dark-photon limit given separately (kinetic mixing, 5e-3..3e1 eV).
evidence: Agent: 1.7e-10 @1.9e-7, 1.6e-10 @3.2e-7, 1.5e-10 @5.2e-7, 9.7e-10 @5.8e-8, 7.9e-10 @1.4e-6 (consistent with the quoted result). GT: DarkPhoton/Crab_2.txt (3.9e-4 @5.3e-3 eV .. 2.4e-2 @31 eV). Different coupling; no comparison.
policy_question: Which of two headline couplings in a two-result paper the compilation records; the agent's ALP choice is not comparable to the DP-only GT.
notes: Transcript: agent noted the paper limits both couplings and chose the ALP result.

verdict: agent right (traced the Fig. 3a curve); curator stores a 2-point flat line at the best value 1.5e-9 and the scorer evaluated the agent's curve at the window edges
my_readings: Fig. 3(a) (linear axes 2.029-2.041 neV): 90% CL limit is a parabola-like curve, minimum 1.5e-9 at 2.035 neV, ~3e-9 at 2.033/2.037, ~5e-9 at 2.030/2.040.
evidence: Agent: min 1.53e-9 @2.0355 neV, 2.9e-9 @2.0319, 4.9e-9 @2.0291/2.0411. GT: 1.5e-9 at 2.031 and 2.039 neV (flat). Scorer residual 0.37 = agent's edge values (3.5-4e-9) vs 1.5e-9 at the two GT masses; the minimum agrees to 0.01 dex.
notes: Same pattern as RADES: headline-value stand-in reference evaluated where the real curve is weakest.

verdict: both defensible: agent reports per-bin log-medians of the jagged FAST limit, curator stores its lower envelope (floor)
my_readings: Fig. 1: solid red FAST curve (randomized polarization, rho=0.3) over 4.14e-6..6.2e-6 eV is a dense jagged band from ~1e-12 (floor) to ~1e-11 with RFI spikes to 1e-8; abstract: 'reach ~1e-12'.
evidence: Agent: 90 bin medians 2.3e-12..1.5e-11, min 1.7e-12. GT (FAST.txt, 239 pts): 1.1e-12..1.9e-12 = the floor of the band. Signed residual +0.32 median (threshold 0.32), p90 0.42. Repo applies sqrt(2/3/0.6) polarisation rescale at plot time, not in the file, so no convention offset.
policy_question: Whether a jagged per-frequency limit is recorded by its lower envelope (curator here) or by a running median (agent); the compilation is not consistent across papers (spiky curves kept for JWST/DD/MuDHI, floor kept here).
notes: Borderline miss (0.321 dex).

verdict: agent and curator trace the same extremely spiky Fig. 11 curve with different sparse samplings (95 vs 74 points); residual is sampling mismatch, not a reading error
my_readings: Fig. 11 (erratum-corrected) magenta MuDHI curve: ~5e-9 @1.1 eV, hundreds of spikes between ~3e-10 and ~1e-7 over 1.3-3.1 eV, sharp notch to ~7e-11 at 1.61 eV (text: 6.86e-11 at 1.61 eV).
notes: Could equally be filed as P (undersampling a curve with hundreds of spikes into 95 points); the GT is itself a 74-point sample of the same curve.

verdict: both defensible: agent emitted the Cas A bound alone (paper's headline, Eq. 37), curator's file is the union 'Cas A + NS1987A' (Eq. 39, stronger but conditional)
my_readings: Fig. 6: red Cas A region lower edge follows eps*m ~ 1.5e-2 eV (1.5e-8 MeV): ~5e-3 @3 eV, ~3e-5 @400 eV, ~1e-7 @5e4 eV, cutoff rising at ~5e5 eV; brown NS1987A region extends below it with eps*m ~ 3e-3 eV (Eq. 39), i.e. a factor 5 lower.
evidence: Agent: 5.2e-3 @2.8, 3.4e-5 @385, 1.1e-7 @5.2e4, 6e-5 @5.3e5 (eps*m = 1.45e-2 eV, = Cas A). GT (NeutronStarCooling.txt, header 'Cas A cooling', docs 'Cas A + NS1987A'): 5.7e-3 @0.51 eV (eps*m = 2.9e-3 eV = NS1987A), 6.1e-7 @3.5e3, then polygon closure vertices. Signed residual +0.69 median = log(5).
policy_question: Whether the compilation's neutron-star-cooling curve is the conservative Cas A bound or the union with the NS1987A bound that the paper itself labels conditional.
notes: Agent notes explicitly weighed NS1987A and chose Cas A as the key result.

verdict: both defensible: agent emitted the paper's opaque fixed-polarisation curve, benchmark GT is the repo's Rescaled/ORGAN-1a.txt (random-polarisation convention)
my_readings: Fig. 1: opaque red (fixed polarisation, |cos theta|^2 ~ 0.03 scenario) floor ~1-3e-12 over 63.2-67.1 ueV; transparent (random polarisation) curve ~3-6e-13, i.e. a factor ~3-5 lower.
policy_question: Which dark-photon polarisation scenario the compilation stores (the repo keeps a Rescaled/ directory in the random-polarisation convention) versus the scenario the paper presents as its main/conservative result.
notes: Agent notes explicitly mention the transparent random-polarisation curve.

verdict: both defensible: paper derives several UFF curves in Fig. 3; agent chose MICROSCOPE Ti/Pt (strongest), benchmark GT is the Eot-Wash EP curve from the same figure
my_readings: Fig. 3 top panel (log10|d_e|): MICROSCOPE Ti/Pt purple flat at ~-4.0 for m < 1e-14 eV rising to leave the frame near 1e-11.5; Eot-Wash Be/Ti orange flat at ~-3.5, rising from ~1e-13, plateau ~-1.4 at 1e-9..1e-6, then rising again.
evidence: Agent: 9.86e-5 flat, 1.7e-4 @1e-13, 4.7e-3 @1.3e-12, exits at 6.4e-12 (= MICROSCOPE). GT (ScalarPhoton/EotWashEP.txt, attributed to this paper): 3.4e-4 flat, 1.2e-3 @5.6e-13, 3.9e-2 plateau @1e-9..3e-7, 59 @3.8e-5 (= Eot-Wash). Coverage 0.19 because the agent's curve ends at the frame exit; where both exist the offset is -0.32..-0.5 dex.
policy_question: Which of the paper's re-derived UFF curves is 'the' limit for this paper: the compilation credits the Eot-Wash recast to this paper and the MICROSCOPE curve to 1712.00483.
notes: Agent explicitly listed the other Fig. 3 curves.

verdict: agent followed the task card (fifth-force paper -> ScalarNucleon with native |alpha|(lambda)); benchmark GT exists only as the compilation's recasts into d_e / d_me (FifthForce.txt), so the sanctioned emission cannot be scored
my_readings: Fig. 5 (p.77 of the review): 95% CL |alpha| vs lambda for 1 um < lambda < 1 cm; envelope of Eot-Wash/Colorado/Stanford/Lamoreaux/Irvine: alpha ~5e-4 at lambda = 1 cm (m = 2e-5 eV), ~1e-2 at 300 um, ~1 at ~50 um, ~1e4 at ~10 um, ~1e10 at ~2.4 um.
evidence: Agent: 5.2e-4 @1.97e-5 eV, 1.1e-2 @7e-5, 0.61 @8.8e-4, 1.3e-4 @1.1e-2 ... 1e10 @8.1e-2 eV, declared 'alpha (Yukawa strength relative to gravity)'. GT: ScalarPhoton/FifthForce.txt and ScalarElectron/FifthForce.txt, 1000-point compilations over 1e-24..1e2 eV built from three references with a model-dependent dilaton-charge recast; no ScalarNucleon file.
notes: The scorer's conventions layer maps native alpha only for ScalarNucleon/VectorBL files with a lambda header; here the GT types themselves are the mismatch. A model-dependent recast (alpha -> d_e) is not something the task card asks the agent to do.

verdict: agent right: its flat g_B = 6.5e-13 equals the curator's ScalarNucleon/WhiteDwarfs.txt value 6.5365e-13 (0.002 dex); it was not scored only because it was labelled ScalarBaryon rather than ScalarNucleon
my_readings: Eq. (4.11a): alpha_B = g_B^2/4pi <= 3.4e-26 -> g_B <= 6.5e-13 (abstract: 7e-13), for L = g_B phi (p-bar p + n-bar n), i.e. g_n = g_p = g_B, flat for m < ~1 keV (Fig. 3 'WD Bremsstrahlung (this work)' flat over 1e-3..1e3 eV).
evidence: Agent: 6.5e-13 flat over 1e-3..1e3 eV, coupling_type ScalarBaryon. GT: ScalarNucleon/WhiteDwarfs.txt 6.5365e-13 flat over 1e-30..1e4 eV (benchmark expected types: ScalarBaryon, ScalarElectron, ScalarNucleon, but only ScalarElectron and ScalarNucleon have files). The task card defines ScalarBaryon as 'coupling of a scalar to baryon number', exactly the paper's wording.
notes: Type aliasing (baryophilic scalar with g_n = g_p vs scalar-nucleon) should be resolved by the scorer, not by the agent.

verdict: both defensible but the agent's lower envelope is optimistic: agent took per-bin minima of the spiky DD bound, curator stores the spiky curve
my_readings: Fig. 2b (g_phigamma [eV^-1]): 'DD current' is a dense spiky band; lower envelope ~4e-20 @1e-14 eV, ~1e-21 @1e-12, ~3e-19 @1e-10, rising to ~1e-15 at 4e-8 eV; spikes reach 1-3 dex above the envelope at DD-sequence harmonics.
evidence: Agent (d_e = g/kappa, kappa = 2.906e-28 eV^-1): 4.3e7 @1.4e-14, 4.2e6 @1.6e-13, 1.9e6 @2e-12, 2.5e6 @6.3e-12, 9.2e6 @2.3e-11 (envelope). GT (DynamicDecoupling.txt, 4.6e-15..3.8e-11 only): 8.3e7 @1.2e-14, 1.1e7 @8.9e-14, 4.3e6 @2.8e-13, 2e8 @8.2e-13 (spike), 2.4e6 @3.1e-12, 8.4e7 @7.7e-12, 7e7 @2.4e-11. Signed median -0.36, max -4.6 at spikes; at non-spike masses agreement is 0.1-0.2 dex.
policy_question: Whether a limit with harmonic sensitivity gaps is recorded as its lower envelope or as the full spiky curve.
notes: Agent notes say 'lower envelope (per-bin minimum), i.e. the strongest bound locally'; the paper states sensitivity is lost at harmonics, so the envelope overstates the exclusion there.

verdict: both defensible: agent emitted the upper envelope (conservative edge) of the jagged 95% CL spectrum; curator traced the spectrum itself, whose typical value is ~1 dex lower
my_readings: Fig. 6 top (log10 d_gamma^(1)): Yb+/Sr 95% C.L. is a dense jagged spectrum ~1 dex tall: at log m = -19 it spans ~-6.0..-5.3; at -18 ~-4.9..-4.3; at -17 ~-4.7..-3.5 (top spikes), with the black dashed expected level at ~-4.5 at -17. Eq. 24: d = 2.0e16 (f/Hz) A_alpha(f).
policy_question: Which edge of a jagged 95% CL spectrum is the compilation boundary: the upper envelope (excluded at every frequency) or the spectrum itself.
notes: Agent notes claim the envelope coincides with the shaded region boundary; the curator evidently did not use that boundary.

verdict: agent followed the task card (Casimir/Yukawa constraints -> native |alpha_G|(lambda) under ScalarNucleon); the only GT is the compilation's model-dependent recast into g_B-L (VectorB-L/Casimir.txt, header: 'compiled from ScalarNucleon/Casimir.txt, rescaled to g_B-L')
my_readings: Sec. 7, Fig. 28: Yukawa constraints |alpha_G| vs lambda from Casimir measurements: curve 6 (AFM, gold) strongest for 4e-9 < lambda < 1.5e-7 m, curve 2 (dielectrics) and curve 4a (Lamoreaux) up to lambda ~ 2e-4 m; alpha_G ~1e13-1e14 at lambda ~ 0.1-0.2 um (m ~ 1-2 eV), ~1e24 at lambda ~ 4 nm (m ~ 50 eV).
evidence: Agent: 4.8e12 @0.81 eV, 1.2e14 @1.6 eV, 8e14 @3.2 eV, 2.4e16 @7.3 eV, 5e19 @21.8 eV, 3.5e24 @49.5 eV (declared native alpha). GT (g_B-L): 3.2e-13 @1.05 eV, 3.4e-12 @3.2 eV, 6.8e-11 @8.3 eV, 1.2e-7 @49.5 eV; converting the GT back with alpha = g^2/(4 pi G m_u^2) gives ~1.4e12 @1 eV, ~1.6e14 @3.2 eV, ~2e17 @49.5 eV vs agent ~1e13, 8e14, 3.5e24: consistent to within the per-nucleon-vs-per-atom normalisation at low mass but diverging by several dex above ~10 eV (different experiments/curves in the two envelopes).
notes: Even with a type alias the curves may not agree at high mass; but the primary reason for the miss is that the sanctioned native-alpha emission has no comparable GT type.

verdict: both defensible: agent reports the centre of the noisy 491k-point limit band (matches the abstract's 1e-25 at 8e-18 eV), curator stores its upper (conservative) envelope, 0.3 dex higher
my_readings: Fig. 5 X-polarisation panel: black band ~0.3 dex thick; centre ~1.1e-25 at the 8e-18 eV minimum, top of band ~2e-25 there; ~5e-25 (centre) at 6e-19 eV; ~2e-24 at 1.5e-16 eV. Abstract: g_B-L < 1e-25 at 8e-18 eV.
policy_question: Centre vs upper envelope of a noisy limit band (and X vs Y vs Z polarisation panel).
notes: Borderline miss (0.302 dex).

verdict: both defensible: agent reports the per-bin median of a limit band that is 1-5 decades wide (in eps^2), curator its upper envelope; conversion g = e*sqrt(eps^2) is the same on both sides
my_readings: Fig. 5 (eps^2_95% vs mass): red low-frequency band ~1e-39..1e-38 at 1e-19..3e-18 eV; black fully-coherent band ~1e-36 @1e-17, ~1e-34 @1e-16, widening to ~1e-30..1e-25 at 2e-15 and up to 1e-22 at 1e-14 eV. With g = 0.303*eps: band at 2e-19 eV spans g ~1e-20..3e-20; at 1.9e-15 eV g ~3e-16..1e-13.
evidence: Agent (band median): 8.3e-21 @2.1e-19, 1.5e-19 @8e-18, 5e-19 @1.1e-16, 2.5e-15 @1.9e-15, 2.8e-13 @1.2e-14. GT (LISAPathfinder.txt): 3.5e-20 @2.2e-19, 6.8e-19 @6.5e-18, 1.2e-17 @1.4e-16, 2.2e-13 @1.9e-15, 6.9e-12 @5.6e-15: consistently at the top of the band (signed -0.9 median, -2 dex at high mass where the band is widest).
policy_question: Which statistic of a very wide noisy limit band (median vs upper envelope) the compilation records; the agent flagged this ambiguity itself (confidence 0.5).
notes: Coupling-type call (VectorBL for the paper's baryon/B-L coupling) agrees with the GT.

verdict: both defensible: the paper is a projection framework (agent: is_projection, no points), but its Appendix E derives an updated MICROSCOPE B-L bound which the compilation adopted as VectorB-L/MICROSCOPE.txt
my_readings: Sec. 3.2 'Projected Exclusions' and Fig. 5: 90% CL projected limits for f0 = 0.1, 1, 10 Hz; Fig. 5 also shows 'MICROSCOPE (First)' and 'MICROSCOPE (Final)', 'the latter of which we compute in Appendix E' ('Updated MICROSCOPE Limit': g_B-L <~ 7e-26 flat below ~1e-14 eV, rising to ~1e-24 at 1e-13 eV per the GT).
evidence: Agent: is_new_limit=false, is_projection=true, data_points=[] (notes explicitly call the MICROSCOPE curve a reinterpretation shown for comparison). GT (VectorB-L/MICROSCOPE.txt, header 'Updated in 2403.02381'): 7.0e-26 flat to ~1e-14 eV, 1.3e-25 @7e-14, 9.2e-25 @2e-13, 7e-19 @1e-12.
policy_question: Whether a recast of another experiment's published EP result inside a projection paper counts as that paper's 'measured limit' for the compilation; the task card's own rule ('reinterpretations ... are not new limits unless the paper derives a new bound itself') is what the agent applied, and the compilation applied the opposite reading.
notes: Agent read Appendix E's existence (mentions the epsilon_B-L recast) and made a considered call; scored as no_extracted_points.

verdict: both defensible: agent traced the blue (optimised T_osc, strongest) region, curator the green (T_osc = 1 keV, 'most conservative') region
policy_question: Which of three nested scenario regions (conservative constant-rate, power-law, optimised T_osc) the compilation records; the caption calls green 'the most conservative bound'.
notes: Agent notes list all three regions and justify choosing the strongest.

summary.method: For every paper the headline figure was rendered from ~/.cache/aal_pdf_cache and 3-5 values read (by eye, or by independent vector-path extraction with tick calibration for 2310.06017, 1401.6460); the values were compared with the agent's result.json points and the benchmark ground-truth file before reading the agent's notes/transcript. arXiv version histories and e-prints were fetched where a version or ancillary-file question arose (2310.06017 v1/v2, 2302.10206 v1, 2402.07976 anc, 2407.16628 single version).
summary.headline: No paper in the 37 shows a perception, conversion or identification error that the paper itself settles (P=C=ID=0). 25 are compilation-policy choices the paper does not fix (which scenario curve, which edge/statistic of a band or spiky curve, which coupling, per-experiment vs envelope, recast-vs-new-limit); 5 are reference-file defects (curator file disagrees with the paper's own figure/axis: 1712.00483, 2201.02042 (Exp. A sensitivity), 2310.06017 (x3.2), 2110.10262 (mislabelled mass axis), 2302.10206); 7 are scorer/GT-coverage artefacts (flat headline stand-ins compared at window edges: RADES, DM-Pathfinder; noisy/spiky-curve sampling: ADBC, MuDHI; type alias ScalarBaryon/ScalarNucleon: 2303.00778; sanctioned native-alpha emissions with no matching GT type: hep-ph/0307284, quant-ph/0106045). Secondary defects noted inside POL entries: 1905.13650 GT stored in GeV^-1 (x2m_n missing, 0.27 dex).
